title: Vanishing of shriek sections near a disjoint closed subset
statement: Let $j:U\to X$ be a weakly etale morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism] and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $U\times_X Z=\varnothing$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $V\to X$ be an affine object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-small-proetale-site] such that every point of $V$ specializes to a point of $V_Z=V\times_X Z$. For every abelian sheaf $G$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] on $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $(j_!G)(V)=0$, where $j_!G$ is the abelian sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of the presheaf $W\mapsto\bigoplus_{\varphi:W\to U\text{ over }X}G(W\xrightarrow{\varphi}U)$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf, lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization].

proof.text: Let P be the opposite localization functor's left Kan extension of G, F its abelian sheafification, and eta : P -> F the sheafification map. Mathlib's Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective instance for eta says that the sieve of arrows on which a section s of F(V) has a representative in P is covering (Presheaf.imageSieve_mem). The underlying set presheaf of F is a sheaf by Presheaf.isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_forget and isSheaf_iff_isSheaf_of_type. Thus we may work directly with abelian sheafification, without constructing its group operations anew.

Given any covering sieve on affine V, extract a generating pro-etale covering family and refine it to finitely many affine open pieces A_j -> V using QuasiCompactCover.exists_isAffineOpen_of_isCompact. These maps are weakly etale by cancellation against V -> X and composition with open immersions. The inverse image C_j of the closed image of i : Z -> X is a closed subset of A_j. Transport C_j across A_j.isoSpec and use PrimeSpectrum.isClosed_iff_zeroLocus_ideal to obtain its arbitrary defining ideal I_j in Gamma(A_j,top). This only needs the closed image of i, not a presentation of the pulled-back closed immersion.

Construct B_j = Spec(Localization S_j), where S_j is the inverse image of the unit submonoid of Gamma(A_j,top)/I_j. The affine closed-specialization localization theorem makes b_j : B_j -> A_j weakly etale, ensures that its image contains every point specializing into C_j, and ensures that every point of B_j specializes inside B_j to a point over C_j. No scheme is chosen from an unproved existence assertion: B_j and b_j are these explicit localizations and spectrum maps. To cover v in V, choose a specialization z in V times_X Z, choose an affine piece A_j over its projection, then use Flat.generalizingMap for A_j -> V to lift the generalization v to a point specializing into C_j. This point lifts to B_j. Hence the finite family B_j -> V is jointly surjective. Its maps are spectral because source and target are affine, so IsCompactOpenCovered.of_finite_of_isSpectralMap verifies the quasi-compact covering condition on each quasi-compact open. Thus it is a pro-etale covering refining the original sieve. Scheme.Pullback.exists_preimage_pullback converts each point over C_j into a point of B_j times_X Z; the specialization property therefore persists in the precise form needed.

For any object W with this specialization property, a lift a : W -> U over X forces W to be empty: a point of W supplies a point of W times_X Z, and the pullback universal property maps that point to the assumed-empty U times_X Z. To show P(W) is zero, use the already-proved final discrete indexing theorem for the pointwise Kan extension. Each canonical comma object has an invertible structure map and induces a lift of W to U. Consequently W is empty and, by that isomorphism, so is the corresponding object T over U. The empty covering makes G(T) zero (isTerminalSectionsOfIsEmpty). The diagram after restriction to the final discrete indexing category is therefore zero, and its colimit P(W) is zero by Functor.Final.isColimitWhiskerEquiv and IsColimit.isZero_pt. This includes empty W without a separate nonempty assumption.

Apply the refinement from steps 2 and 3 to the image sieve of s from step 1. On each B_j the representative p_j is zero by step 4. Naturality and preservation of zero by the sheafification map give s restricted to B_j = 0. The separatedness part of the underlying set sheaf condition on this covering gives s = 0. Thus every two sections coincide. The finite-family argument also admits the empty family, so empty V is covered.
